text:
alex: FYI ran into a weird installer edge on Alpine containers -> the prebuilt redwoodctl (glibc) exits with `No such file or directory` even though binary is present. musl vs glibc problem. Anyone added an Alpine-compatible build?

mei: we only ship glibc artifacts by default. for the localtest slim images we should publish a musl build or a static linked binary. short-term: use `gcompat` layer in the container or switch to debian slim.

raul: two follow-ups: 1) the macOS Homebrew package is marked keg-only in our formula which breaks `brew link` for devs who expect `redwoodctl` on PATH; 2) our installer writes a ~/.redwood/credentials file with 0600 perms but on windows the path ends up in "C:\Users\USER\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\credentials" and the installer sometimes creates it as read-only (CI mounted volume). Users hit permission denied after upgrade.

tess: for (1) can we make formula non-keg-only for the cask/dev channel and add a shim? I had a new hire spend 30m debugging PATH. For (2) we should ensure installer checks and fixes file flags post-write and print a clear error when permissions prevent token refresh.

alex: another annoying DX bug: `redwoodctl config profile set` silently truncates very long profile names (we sanitize to 32 chars) and then all SDKs fail because the CLI writes truncated names and our SDKs expect full name. Repro: `redwoodctl config profile create "enterprise-long-name-company-prod"` -> stored as "enterprise-long-name-company-pr".

mei: that's a surprising one. why are we truncating? Probably ancient constraint from legacy UI. We should validate and reject too-long names rather than silently trimming. Will add validation + migrate fix to rename collisions.

raul: onboarding sample app note: the quickstart uses `redwoodctl login` but the sample app's README assumes device auth. New hires end up doing browser flow and hitting corporate SSO popup that fails inside the dev VM. We should align quickstart to `redwoodctl login --device` for headless-friendly instructions and show both flows.

alex: auth caching: token cache TTL is 10m but we treat 401 as trigger to refresh. CI flakes because cached token is valid but backend returns 401 for a short window during key rotation. CLI should do one immediate fallback to refresh then fail fast with an exit code for non-interactive. Right now it retries 4x with delays and blocks pipelines.

tess: agreed. propose: if not tty -> no interactive retry, exit 74 + JSON hint. If interactive -> do one silent refresh attempt then prompt. Also add telemetry event so we can correlate flakes with rotation windows.

release-bot: NOTE: Created issues: #4601 (build: publish musl/static binary for alpine), #4602 (installer: fix homebrew keg-only & windows perms), #4603 (config: reject long profile names), #4604 (docs: quickstart switch to device auth), #4605 (auth: CI-friendly retry behavior + telemetry).

mei: I'll pick up #4601 and #4605. Will also drop a tiny README change for quickstart device flow. Thanks for the signal. :raised_hands:
